record.original_question: Suppose a II_1 factor M decomposes as a tensor product M ≅ N_1 ⊗ N_2 and M is McDuff. Must at least one of the tensor factors N_1 or N_2 also be McDuff?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. If M ∼= N1⊗N2, and M is McDuff, does it imply that either N1 or N2 are McDuff ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A II$_1$ factor is a separable, infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebra $M$ with trivial center and a (unique) faithful normal tracial state $\tau$. Let $R$ denote the hyperfinite II$_1$ factor. A II$_1$ factor $M$ is called McDuff if $M \cong M \,\overline{\otimes}\, R$.

Suppose that a II$_1$ factor $M$ admits a tensor product decomposition $M \cong N_1 \,\overline{\otimes}\, N_2$, where $N_1$ and $N_2$ are II$_1$ factors, and assume that $M$ is McDuff. Must at least one of $N_1$ or $N_2$ be McDuff?
artifact.status_search_result: The question whether McDuffness of a tensor product II$_1$ factor forces one of the tensor factors to be McDuff appears to be a well-known structural question in von Neumann algebras. Related results exist on uniqueness of McDuff decompositions (e.g., Boutonnet–Ioana–Salehi-Golsefidy and follow-up work) and on central sequence algebras of tensor products, but no source located confirms a complete resolution of the question in general. Status appears unknown/open based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: A class of II_1 factors with a unique McDuff decomposition
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a large class of II_1 factors N such that N ⊗ R has a unique McDuff decomposition, but does not resolve the general tensor splitting question.
status_evidence.claim: Related uniqueness results exist for McDuff decompositions, but the general question whether a McDuff tensor product forces one factor to be McDuff is not settled there.

status_evidence.title: On central sequence algebras of tensor product von Neumann algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies central sequence algebras of tensor products M ⊗ N, addressing related but distinct structural questions.
status_evidence.claim: Active research into central sequences of tensor products does not resolve the stated problem.
